clue.text: Expert whose clients are relieved to go under

definitions.text: Expert whose clients are relieved to go under

parts.words: Expert whose clients are relieved to go under
parts.note: seems to describe a debt adviser whose clients are glad to go bankrupt, but 'relieved' means freed from pain and 'go under' means lose consciousness

explanation.surface: A financial adviser whose clients are thankful when their businesses collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go under' looks like business failure; in the operating theatre it means slipping into unconsciousness, and the relief is from pain.
explanation.definitionFit: The specialist doctor who puts patients to sleep before surgery is the one whose patients go under.

clue.text: Talking bird taking no time turning up — or the opposite

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the whole thing reads from the bottom upwards
the bird taking a piece means the bird holds it inside itself

parts.note: the mynah or myna is a bird famous for mimicking speech
taken as written

explanation.surface: A talking bird fails to keep time and turns up, or doesn't.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' puts NOT inside MYNA to give MYNOTNA; 'turning up' turns that round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A word of contrary meaning is called its opposite, as hot is to cold.

clue.text: A gin knocked back on one's own

indicators.note: knocked back suggests drinking, but here it sends the word for a snare backwards

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for catching animals

explanation.surface: Someone downs a gin alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' looks like the drink, which 'knocked back' supports; it is the snare, and 'knocked back' reverses TRAP to PART.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set aside from others, or separately, is what being on one's own means.

clue.text: Have misgivings seeing Ella in unusually smart surroundings

indicators.note: the rearranged word forms the surroundings that hold the name Ella
unusually means the letters of smart are set out in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grows suspicious on seeing Ella somewhere oddly posh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' reads as the posh setting, but with 'unusually' it is anagram fodder (SMRAT), split by 'surroundings' around the name.
explanation.definitionFit: To sense that something is wrong is an idiom for being suspicious or having doubts.

clue.text: No end of vacs — third of theirs and mine

indicators.note: no end of means the final letter of the word for vacs is dropped

parts.note: vacs (vacations) are holidays, in British slang hols

indicators.note: third of picks the third letter of the word theirs

explanation.surface: Endless vacuuming, with a share of theirs and mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' looks like 'lots of'; it cuts the last letter from HOLS, the British student word for vacations.
explanation.definitionFit: A mine is a pit dug into the ground, an excavated opening.

clue.text: Involved university in sort-out for transport

indicators.note: university in the rest means its letter goes inside
transport means carry away, so the letters of sort-out are carried into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A university gets involved in reorganising its transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for transport' jumbles SORTOUT into TORTOUS, and 'in' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something convoluted or complicated, like a long-winded argument, can be called involved.

clue.text: Staff in more ways than one

definitions.text: Staff in more ways than one

parts.words: Staff in more ways than one
parts.note: staff is both a stick or pole and the five-line music staff, and the answer means both

explanation.surface: A cryptic hint that the word staff has several meanings.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a wooden rod and also the lines on which music is written, both called a staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A stout stick and the set of lines for musical notation are both names for a staff.

clue.text: Weapon at disposal of one mob after another?

indicators.note: disposal means arranging, so the doubled word is set out in a new order

parts.note: one mob after another gives the word mob twice in succession

explanation.surface: A weapon is handed to one gang after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one mob after another' gives the word twice, and 'disposal of' scrambles the pair into OMBOMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear fission device dropped on cities is a weapon of mass destruction.

clue.text: Cutting edge arts festival?

definitions.meaning: hair cut straight across the forehead, a trimmed edge
the Edinburgh ..., the famous open-access arts festival held alongside the main festival

explanation.surface: An avant-garde arts festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting edge' reads as avant-garde but means an edge of cut hair over the brow.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair trimmed over the forehead and the alternative Edinburgh arts event share this name.

clue.text: Retreat of republican French female, facing cunning agent selling out

indicators.note: retreat means go backwards, so the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: elle is French for she
V, short for versus, means facing or against
art means craft or cunning

explanation.surface: A republican Frenchwoman withdraws, confronting a crafty spy who has sold out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat of' reverses the whole string RELLEVART. 'agent selling out' is a sales rep out on the road, not a turncoat spy.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial salesman who goes out on the road visiting customers was called a commercial traveller.

clue.text: Animated bubbly Romeo

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A lively Romeo full of fizz.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up and about, active and stirring, is to be animated.

clue.text: Sting's roots let out by Geordieland tango

parts.note: Geordies come from Newcastle in north-east England, NE
Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: out means the letters of let are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: The singer Sting's Tyneside roots, revealed by a tango from Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting the singer is a Geordie from Newcastle, which makes the surface. 'out' rearranges LET to TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: This plant stings, and to irritate or provoke someone is also to sting them.

clue.text: Splendid chap and archetypal hero

parts.note: super means splendid or excellent
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A fine fellow who is also a classic hero.
explanation.definitionFit: The caped comic-book character is the model for every later costumed hero.

clue.text: Taking two-thirds some agree would be inadequate

indicators.note: the phrase some agree has nine letters and six of them, two-thirds, are taken from inside it

explanation.surface: Two-thirds agreeing would not be enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking two-thirds' looks like a fraction of a vote; it takes six of the nine letters of 'some agree'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scanty or insufficient amount is described as poor or inadequate.

clue.text: Parable of galley rowed unyoked at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: yoked means wed, so un-yoked removes the letters spelling wed from the word rowed

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A story of a galley rowed without yokes on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unyoked' takes WED (yoked) from ROWED, leaving RO; 'at sea' rearranges GALLEY plus RO.
explanation.definitionFit: A story with a hidden moral meaning, like a parable, is an extended metaphor of this kind.

clue.text: Force for something stronger than a catnap?

definitions.meaning: to force or push something through by sheer power
a cat's nap is a short doze, and a bull is a stronger beast than a cat, so a bull's doze

explanation.surface: A force more powerful than a short sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer's two halves: a bull outstrips a cat, and a doze is a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing through regardless of opposition, as with an earth-moving machine, is to force.

clue.text: Local Cockney actor poolside

parts.note: a lido is an open-air public swimming pool
Michael Caine is the actor famous for his Cockney accent

explanation.surface: A Cockney actor sitting by the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is short for local anaesthetic, not a pub or a resident.
explanation.definitionFit: A local anaesthetic numbs one area; this drug, used by dentists, is one.

clue.text: Grand artist with loud following — one leading to work like Banksy's?

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword artist
f, forte, is the musical direction for loud
f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A great artist with a noisy following leading the way to Banksy-style work.
explanation.walkthrough: Banksy is the anonymous British street artist; a single piece of such wall writing is a graffito.
explanation.definitionFit: A single drawing or scribble on a wall is the singular of a word for street art.

clue.text: Quite regularly checks pay, which is useful

indicators.note: checks means holds back or contains, so the pay holds the picked letters

parts.note: a salary is regular pay

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word Quite

explanation.surface: Fairly routine checks on pay are worthwhile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'checks' looks like inspections; it means holds in, so the pay word contains the letters 'regularly' picks from Quite.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beneficial or good for you, like a sharp lesson, is helpful and useful.

clue.text: Some way to go with two noughts missing from school record

indicators.note: missing from means those letters are taken out of school

parts.note: taken as written
a nought looks like the letter O, so two of them are OO
an EP, extended play, is a kind of record

explanation.surface: A long way to go when a school record lacks two zeros.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing from' removes the two O's from SCHOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tedious, tiring trek is a Yiddish-derived term for a long way to go.

clue.text: Wholesome? It's plausible denied calmer exterior

indicators.note: denied means the plausible word goes without those letters

parts.note: credible means believable or plausible

indicators.note: exterior picks the outside letters of the word calmer

explanation.surface: Is it healthy? The plausible story is refused a calmer face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exterior' takes CR from calmer, and 'denied' removes those from CREDIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is fit to eat is, loosely, wholesome; the question mark flags the stretch.

clue.text: Feature of Cockney intellectual?

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the initial H, so the word is heard as he would say it

parts.note: a highbrow is an intellectual

explanation.surface: What distinguishes a brainy Londoner?
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class East Londoners, drop their H's, so HIGHBROW comes out as 'IGHBROW.
explanation.definitionFit: The arch of hair above each eye is one of the features of a face.

clue.text: Work for aircrew in chic society?

definitions.meaning: an airman's working life is spent at altitude, a life up high

explanation.surface: Flight crew jobs within the fashionable set.
explanation.definitionFit: The glamorous existence of the rich and fashionable is known by this phrase.

clue.text: Sir Tim's creation, part in comfortably rich West End theatre?

definitions.meaning: Sir Tim Rice writes the words for musicals
the Lyric is a theatre on Shaftesbury Avenue in London's West End

indicators.note: part in means the letters are a part found inside the words comfortably rich

explanation.surface: Sir Tim's work plays a part in a well-off West End theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Tim Rice wrote the words for Evita and Jesus Christ Superstar; the West End is London's theatre district.
explanation.definitionFit: Words of a song are what a lyricist like Tim Rice creates, and London has a theatre of this name.

clue.text: Peculiar cyst he cut

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, so the letters are put in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: He had a strange cyst removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like part of the story but is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To mow or slice with a long curved blade is to cut.

clue.text: Complete wreck

definitions.meaning: absolute or utter, as in a complete disaster
to write off a car, destroying it completely

explanation.surface: An utter wreck.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter and entire both mean complete, and smashing a car beyond repair is to wreck it.

clue.text: Fancy Women's Institute over-50s

parts.note: the WI is the Women's Institute, a British community organisation
L is the Roman numeral fifty, so two fifties give LL

explanation.surface: The Women's Institute appeals to the over-50s.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a British countrywide club for women, popularly linked with older members.
explanation.definitionFit: To wish for or desire something is to fancy it, as in 'as you will'.

clue.text: Mistake denying bully 90-year-old British fizz

indicators.note: denying means the bully goes without the drink's letters

parts.note: a terrorizer is one who bullies through fear
Tizer is a British fizzy soft drink launched in 1924

explanation.surface: A mistake was refusing a bully some old British pop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'denying' takes T from the front and IZER from the end of TERRORIZER. Tizer is a red fizzy drink sold in Britain since 1924.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder or slip is a mistake.

clue.text: Irritation right away brought about by pioneer

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, so the remaining letters are rearranged
away means that letter is sent off from the word Irritation

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Annoyance at once caused by a pioneer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' takes one R out of IRRITATION, and 'brought about' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who starts something off, a founder or trailblazer, is a pioneer.

clue.text: Classmate that's in the same swimming group

definitions.meaning: a pupil at the same school as you

definitions.text: that's in the same swimming group
definitions.meaning: a school is a group of fish swimming together, so a fish beside you in it is a fellow member

explanation.surface: A classmate who is also in the same swim team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming group' sounds like a swim club; it is a school of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil who attends the same school as you is a classmate.
